text:
alex: heads-up — saw a weird throughput dip on Mistral-7B dedicated pool after the latest runtime kernel swap. p50 ok, p99 spikes.

alex: baseline before the swap (kv dims=64, num_kv_heads=8, MQA): throughput 420 tok/s, p99=48ms; after swap (new fused-attn kernel): throughput 360 tok/s, p99=120ms. short logs attached below.

alex: stacktrace-ish: `serve:warp: kernel_select -> fused_attn_v2` then sudden increase in nvprof sm_efficiency variance.

jen: did we change any batching heuristics at the same time?

tariq: not intentionally. the deploy included kernel hint and an aggressive batching bump: max_batch_size 64 -> 96 for that pool.

maria: MQA vs GQA knobs? the workloads on that pool are mixed (chat + long contexts). we might be hitting paged KV fragmentation when context length > 4k.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: job=kv-paged-frag-run-19187, metric=throughput, delta=-14.3%, error_budget=within-warning. link: https://ci.redwood/bench/kv-paged-frag-run-19187

tariq: here's a quick profile snippet (top lines):
```
CPU: scheduler stalls ~12%
GPU: active occupancy ~72% -> 55% during spike
KV cache: page faults rising from 0.2/s -> 3.8/s
RoPE: scale factor adjust flag OFF -> some models show token drift
```

jen: hmm page faults from paged-KV rising is a red flag. that correlates with fragmentation. if small allocations scatter across pages, we lose coalesced GPU loads and kernel becomes memory-bound.

maria: also saw RoPE amplitude drift for Mixtral at >6k context in e2e eval. could be related: when caching slices across page boundaries rotary interpolation loses continuity, causing attention kernels to take extra compute and fallback paths.

alex: proposed quick triage steps: 1) rollback batching bump to 64 for that pool 2) force kernel_select to prefer legacy tiled-kernel for Mistral as a canary 3) add KV compaction pass during low traffic windows

tariq: I can push (1) and (2) to canary cluster now. want me to also pin num_key_value_heads to 16 for the canary? It may reduce per-head kv dim but align better with the fused kernel assumptions.

jen: pin to 16 for canary if workloads are mainly MQA -> that reduces head stride mismatch. note: for Llama-like configs we usually keep 8 heads *higher kv dim*, for Qwen we lean to 16. this pool is mixed.

maria: small experiment idea: increase kv_dim from 64 -> 128 while keeping total kv params constant by halving num_heads; observe if cache packing improves (fewer pages, larger contiguous entries).

alex: important: make sure to run the microbench harness after changes. runtime-ci, can you kick the frag microbench against canary? include both long-context chat (8k) and churny short sessions (avg 80 tokens, TTL 30s).

runtime-ci: started: https://ci.redwood/testruns/191876/frag-canary-1. Tests: long-context-8k, churny-short-ttl30. ETA ~12m.

perf-bot: quick note: previous regressions in Jan were fixed by packing KV entries to 256B boundaries. check `kv_pack_align=256` from rollout-0.9.

tariq: ack. will enable `kv_pack_align=256` on canary too. also toggling `kv_compact_threshold=0.25` to trigger compaction earlier.

jen: keep an eye on RoPE scaling flag — if we see token-level quality regressions after compaction, we may need to enable continuity-preserving compaction (move whole token spans, not arbitrary slices).

maria: FYI test run shows initial improvement after rollback of batch bump: throughput recovered to ~410 tok/s but p99 still at ~70ms for long-context. fragmentation metric down 60%.

alex: good. next: if pinned kernels + pack align fixes p99 under 60ms we can roll. otherwise we need to dig into kernel memory coalescing assumptions (maybe update warp-aligned loads).

tariq: action items: (a) canary patch: batching=64, kernel_prefer=legacy_tiled, kv_pack_align=256, kv_compact_threshold=0.25 (b) experiment: head/dim swap (num_kv_heads 8->16, kv_dim 64->32 and kv_dim 64->128 swap tests) (c) perf harness run — runtime-ci running.

jen: also add a short eval to check RoPE continuity after compaction: run mixtral-rope-check on 8k windows, compare logits/embedding drift.

runtime-ci: frag-canary-1 complete. results: churny-short -> throughput +2%, p99 stable; long-context-8k -> throughput +8%, p99 down 18%. detailed logs: https://ci.redwood/testruns/191876/frag-canary-1/logs

maria: promising. but still seeing isolated 500ms stalls when a particular user's session triggers page boundary crossing at token 4128.

alex: assign to tariq for further kernel/profile deep-dive. @tariq can you pick this up today and sync with maria on the RoPE continuity test?

tariq: on it. will also open a perf ticket and drop the nvprof traces + kernel traces there. ticket: PERF-9872.

jen: thanks - let's keep the canary running for 24h before broad rollout. :thumbsup:

alex: perfect. update here once ticket or canary passes.
